items.name: Claude (Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5)
items.description: Current Claude 5 family; owner uses it via the Claude CLI subscription for scripts, agents and the command chat.
items.why: Keep using via the existing subscription (zero marginal cost); check current API pricing on anthropic.com before any API use.

extra.note: Third-party price lists citing 4.x models were stale and dropped.

items.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro / GPT-5.2
items.description: Reseller lists GPT-5.2 $1.75/$14 and Gemini 3.1 Pro $2/$12 per M tokens.
items.why: Not needed given Claude subscription; unverified reseller prices.

items.name: Qwen3.5 9B (Q4_K_M)
items.description: Top 8GB local pick (~5.7GB, ~38 tok/s); Qwen3.5 4B 2.7GB for CPU/long context.
items.why: Best local drafting model on the 4060; keep context 4-8K.

items.name: Gemma 4 (E4B / 12B QAT)
items.description: Writing-quality alternative; 12B QAT ~6.6GB, E4B small; sources conflict on sizes.
items.why: Try for prose; verify variant sizes.

items.name: Health Connect Jetpack client (androidx.health.connect:connect-client)
items.description: Android's on-device health data hub API: read/write steps, exercise, sleep, mindfulness sessions etc. 1.1.0 stable includes MindfulnessSessionRecord (WRITE_MINDFULNESS, experimental opt-in, needs FEATURE_MINDFULNESS_SESSION check).
items.why: Standard offline way for a native Android app to share fitness/mindful minutes with the rest of the phone; needs a privacy-rationale activity in the manifest.

items.name: Local Deep Research
items.description: Local multi-step research assistant with citations: quick summaries, detailed reports, document analysis over your own files (encrypted per-user SQLCipher library). Runs on Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM, or cloud models; free search via SearXNG, arXiv, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, Wikipedia, GitHub; REST/Python API and a local STDIO MCP server for Claude Code. 8,270 commits, last commit 2026-10-16.
items.verdictNote: trial: research reports at $0 on a local 9B model
items.why: Fills the 'topic to cited report' step at zero API cost; self-reported SimpleQA 91.2% with Qwen3.5-9B (95.7% with a 27B model on a 24 GB card), small sample and LLM-graded. Docker on Windows needs the port-mapped compose; egress guard is best-effort and self-hosted SearXNG still forwards queries upstream; back up before upgrading (v1.10.7 warning).

items.name: React Three Rapier
items.description: Rapier (WASM) physics for React Three Fiber: rigid bodies, colliders, joints, collision events. v2 needs @react-three/fiber v9 and React 19 (v1 for React 18). Last commit 2025-11-03.
items.verdictNote: conditional on a React Three Fiber stack
items.why: Easiest physics for R3F games. Commit activity has slowed (last Nov 2025). For non-React three.js games use Rapier's own JS package directly.

items.name: Yuka
items.description: Engine-agnostic JavaScript game-AI library: state- and goal-driven agents, steering behaviours, graphs and navmesh pathfinding, perception with memory and vision, triggers, fuzzy logic, JSON save/load.
items.verdictNote: assess: good design, no commits since 2023
items.why: Works with any web engine, including a custom one. Last commit 2023-01-16, so expect no fixes; small and readable enough to vendor and maintain yourself if adopted.

items.name: three.quarks
items.description: Particle and VFX system for three.js (sparks, smoke, trails, magic) with a WYSIWYG editor at quarks.art that exports JSON. WebGPU rendering still on the roadmap. Last commit 2026-05-20.
items.why: Fills a real gap: designed effects without hand-writing shaders. Editor pricing not stated; WebGL only for now.

items.name: Colyseus
items.description: Authoritative multiplayer framework for Node.js: rooms, matchmaking, reconnection and automatic state sync, with client SDKs for JavaScript, Unity, Godot, Defold and Construct. Pre-1.0; last commit 2026-10-16.
items.verdictNote: assess when a multiplayer game is planned
items.why: MIT and self-hostable, so the cost is the server it runs on; the maintainers' paid Colyseus Cloud (pricing not shown) funds the project. Multiplayer adds hosting, cheating and moderation work: only worth it for a game designed around it.

items.name: Semantic Router
items.description: Routes a request to a predefined workflow by embedding similarity instead of asking an LLM to decide; works with local embedding models. Last commit 2026-10-19.
items.why: Replaces an LLM classification call with a near-free embedding lookup; needs good example utterances per route and a fallback when nothing matches.

items.name: RouteLLM
items.description: Trained routers that send easier prompts to a cheaper model and harder ones to a stronger model.
items.why: Last commit 2024-08-10; its routers were trained on an older strong/weak model pair. A rules-plus-fallback tier chain in LiteLLM is simpler and measurable.

items.name: GPTCache
items.description: Semantic cache for LLM answers: reuses a stored answer when a new request is similar enough. Last commit 2026-09-22.
items.verdictNote: assess: only for truly repetitive questions
items.why: A wrong 'similar enough' match returns a confidently stale or wrong answer. Use LiteLLM's built-in cache first; add semantic matching only where requests really repeat and freshness rules are clear.

items.name: requests-cache
items.description: Drop-in persistent cache for Python requests with expiry rules per URL. Last commit 2026-10-15.
items.why: One line stops scripts re-downloading the same public API data; set expiry per source so prices and news stay fresh.

items.name: Hishel
items.description: HTTP caching and revalidation (ETag/Last-Modified) for the Python httpx client. Last commit 2026-10-05.
items.why: Same job as requests-cache for httpx; pick the one matching the HTTP client a script already uses.

items.name: Chonkie
items.description: Lightweight document chunking library (token, sentence, semantic and other chunkers) for retrieval pipelines. Last commit 2026-08-26.
items.why: Sending the relevant chunks instead of whole documents is one of the largest token savings; only matters once there is a document-search step.

items.name: FlagEmbedding (BGE)
items.description: BAAI's BGE embedding and reranker models plus training code; rerankers re-score retrieved passages so only the strongest evidence reaches the prompt. Last commit 2026-08-24.
items.why: Reranking before generation cuts prompt size and improves accuracy. Check each model card's licence and VRAM; the smaller rerankers are expected to fit an 8 GB GPU (not measured).

items.name: LLMLingua
items.description: Microsoft's prompt compression (LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua, LLMLingua-2) that drops low-information tokens before the model reads them. Last commit 2026-09-10.
items.verdictNote: assess against a golden set first
items.why: Compression can silently drop numbers, negations and conditions. Only keep it where a before/after test on real tasks shows no accuracy loss; fix oversized inputs upstream first.

items.name: Prefect
items.description: Python workflow orchestration with retries, scheduling and task-result caching keyed on inputs; optional paid Prefect Cloud. Last commit 2026-10-19.
items.verdictNote: skip while n8n is the orchestrator
items.why: Good for code-heavy Python pipelines, but duplicates n8n plus a database job queue for a no-code-first setup.

items.name: Celery
items.description: Distributed Python task queue; needs a broker such as Redis or RabbitMQ. Last commit 2026-10-18.
items.why: Adds a broker to run and monitor; a database-backed job queue driven by n8n covers the same need at this scale.

items.name: APScheduler
items.description: In-process Python job scheduler (cron, interval, date triggers). Last commit 2026-10-13.
items.why: Handy inside a standalone Python script; n8n schedules already cover workflow timing.

items.name: PyBreaker
items.description: Circuit breaker for Python: stops calling a failing service after a threshold, then retries after a cool-off. Last commit 2026-09-25.
items.why: The pattern matters (stop runaway retry loops); for model calls LiteLLM's allowed-fails and cooldown settings already do it. Use PyBreaker only for non-LLM services called from Python.

items.name: Portkey Gateway
items.description: Open-source AI gateway with routing, fallbacks, retries and caching across many providers; hosted Portkey adds paid features. Last commit 2026-05-25.
items.why: Overlaps LiteLLM almost entirely; running two gateways doubles the configuration for no saving.

items.name: Listmonk
items.why: Self-hosted newsletter and mailing-list manager already running for several brands; pair it with an external SMTP provider (SES/SMTP2GO) plus SPF/DKIM/DMARC.

items.name: short-video-maker
items.why: Open-source short-video assembler (Kokoro TTS, Whisper captions, Remotion) that matches our local stack; check how actively it is maintained and Remotion's licence terms.

items.name: PocketBase
items.why: Single Go binary (SQLite) providing auth, storage, realtime and a REST API in about 30 MB; a lighter backend option for new small apps than a full Supabase stack.

items.name: Ruflo (formerly Claude Flow)
items.description: Agent 'meta-harness' for Claude Code and Codex, renamed from claude-flow: 100+ agents, swarm topologies, vector memory, federation across machines, a large MCP server (about 300 tools) and hundreds of skills. Installs via npx or a Claude Code plugin. Very active (commit 2026-10-24).
items.verdictNote: reference: study the swarm and memory patterns; don't install into your main setup
items.why: Huge surface and many claims (routing accuracy, security hardening) with no evidence on the page; the README itself says plugins run unsandboxed with your permissions. Hundreds of MCP tools also bloat every session's context. Claude Code's own sub-agents cover most needs for less.

items.name: CLI-Anything
items.description: Generates agent-friendly command-line interfaces for existing desktop software, with structured output. CLI-Hub installs community harnesses for Blender, ComfyUI, Audacity, QGIS, Calibre, Dify, ChromaDB and more; a seven-phase pipeline builds new ones from source. Plugins for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Last commit 2026-09-22.
items.verdictNote: trial: try one ready-made harness (Blender or ComfyUI) before generating your own
items.why: Lets an agent drive creative apps without screen clicking, which is cheaper and more reliable than computer use. Harness quality varies by contributor (research-lab project), so test each one on a throwaway file first.

items.name: ai-memory
items.description: Shared long-term memory for coding agents: a git-backed wiki of plain markdown (source of truth) plus a rebuildable SQLite search index. Works with 20+ harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro) via MCP or hooks. Rust single binary or Docker; Linux and macOS, Windows through WSL2. Optional LLM or embedding API keys. Last commit 2026-10-22.
items.verdictNote: assess: worth it only if you switch between several coding agents and want one memory
items.why: Sound design: readable markdown in git, so nothing is locked in a database. Adds a service to run, and native Windows is experimental. If you mostly use one agent, its built-in memory or a CLAUDE.md is simpler.

items.name: Context Mode
items.description: MCP server plus hooks that keep large tool outputs (logs, web pages, Playwright snapshots, issue lists) out of the agent's context: commands run in a sandboxed subprocess, results are indexed in local SQLite full-text search, and only matching snippets come back. Also logs session events so the agent can recover after compaction. Supports Claude Code and 16 other agents; best with Claude Code hooks. Vendor claims up to 98% context savings (not independently verified). Very active (commit 2026-10-24).
items.verdictNote: trial: one week on a long Claude Code project; compare session length and cost
items.why: Targets the real cost driver in long agent sessions: bulky tool output. Everything stays local. Elastic License 2.0 is fine for your own use but forbids offering it to others as a hosted service.

items.name: agentic-framework (JeweledTech)
items.description: Python framework that arranges AI agents into business departments (sales, marketing, engineering, support, back office) with optional CrewAI, a FastAPI server, Docker, a demo UI and a library of n8n workflow templates. About 24 commits; last commit 2026-05-12.
items.verdictNote: skip: early, stale since May and marketing-heavy
items.why: Headline numbers (departments, 87 workflows) are unproven and there's an enterprise upsell. Claude's plugins plus n8n give the same department setup with less code to maintain. The n8n templates may be worth a look.

items.name: AI-Powered-Digital-Marketing-Agency (Amanux7)
items.description: Small prototype: React/Vite front end and one Python file where specialist agents draft marketing work that an 'AI CMO' agent reviews. 11 files, 4 commits; last 2026-01-09.
items.why: Only the reviewer-agent idea is worth keeping (one agent checks the others before delivery); there's nothing here to install.
